properties.decision: Recorded as BRAINSTORMING, not as a proposal — dev_storyflow field report 2026-09-05, wish #29. The reporter's sequencing decision split an epoch — Y0-Y2 before increment 2, Y3+X+Z after increment 3 — and 'a DesignEpoch carries one position. There is no honest way to draw it: precedes on the epoch would assert something false about half of it.' They recorded the split in decision text and noted on the governed_by edge that the epoch must eventually be divided. The idea: a DECOMPOSES edge between epochs (parent increment -> two child increments) so the plan can SAY it rather than narrate it. WHAT IS CHEAP: DECOMPOSES already exists; the change is endpoint enumeration (DesignEpoch -> DesignEpoch), the same one-line shape as the SCHEDULED_FOR finding.
properties.name: OPEN — a sequencing decision that SPLITS an increment cannot be drawn: a DesignEpoch has one position. Should DECOMPOSES between DesignEpochs let a plan say 'this increment becomes two'?
properties.rationale: THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: dec:arrival-delta computes an epoch's delta against its FIRST snapshot and refuses a lossy schedule edit — and splitting an epoch IS a schedule edit. The arrival semantics of a parent whose children arrive separately must be defined before the edge is allowed, or arrival_delta computes against a whole that no longer exists. A real design question, not a schema line. Same family as wish #7 (a Decision cannot be scheduled) and fact:defect-a-planned-verification-cannot-be-scheduled...: the plan vocabulary is thinner than the plans people actually make.
